comments.body: I did not manage to reproduce this, but it was a real phenomenon during Penpot development; it occurred several times.

I could not reproduce this live (no Clojure / clojure-lsp setup in this session), but tracing Serena's own caching layer narrows where the staleness has to come from.

`LSPFileBuffer.contents` (`src/solidlsp/ls.py:152-167`) re-reads the file from disk whenever `mtime` has advanced, and `content_hash` (`:180-183`) is derived from that content, so `_raw_document_symbols_cache` and `_document_symbols_cache` (both keyed on `content_hash`) correctly miss and re-query the language server after any on-disk edit. That part looks sound, Serena's own cache is not serving stale data here.

The gap is on the language server's side of that re-query. `LSPFileBuffer._open_in_ls` (`:120-136`) sends `didOpen` exactly once per buffer, guarded by `_is_open_in_ls` (`:124-126`). Buffers are ref-counted and reused across calls while any caller still holds them open (`open_file`, `:1264-1271`), so a later `find_symbol` call on an already-open file is a no-op there. The only two places in this file that send `didChange` are `insert_text_at_position` (`:1342`) and `delete_text_between_positions` (`:1385`), Serena's own edit tools. `grep -n "did_change_text_document\|did_open_text_document" src/solidlsp/ls.py src/solidlsp/language_servers/clojure_lsp.py` returns only those three call sites, nothing clojure-specific.

So if `nodes.cljc` was already open in the LS session and changed on disk by something other than Serena's own edit calls (an external editor, a checkout, a rebuild), Serena's Python side correctly notices the mtime change and issues a fresh `documentSymbol` request, but nothing tells clojure-lsp the buffer changed. The response can still reflect clojure-lsp's own last-known document state. That matches the shape in the log: `make-nested` reported at lines 206-215 (a comment block ending right before a different function's `defn-`) while its real body is at 454, i.e. the position clojure-lsp associated with that name before the file moved around it.

What I have not checked: whether clojure-lsp does its own filesystem watching independent of the client (some servers register `workspace/didChangeWatchedFiles` or poll on their own), which would close this gap regardless of what Serena sends. If it does, this is not the mechanism. Flagging it as a lead worth a targeted test (open a file in an LS session, edit it via a bare write instead of `insert_text_at_position` / `delete_text_between_positions`, then re-query `find_symbol` in the same session) rather than a confirmed cause.

Building on @AmirF194's trace rather than repeating it — their read of the cache layer matches what I see, and I think I can close the specific question they flagged as unchecked.

> What I have not checked: whether clojure-lsp does its own filesystem watching independent of the client

Serena does not rely on the server doing that: `LanguageServerManager` already sends `workspace/didChangeWatchedFiles` for exactly this case (`src/serena/ls_manager.py:296-356`), with a docstring naming the scenario precisely — *"edits made through any other channel (another editor, a second agent, a git checkout, a build step) are otherwise invisible to a warm language server, causing symbolic queries to answer from a stale index."*

So the external-edit path is handled in general. **But clojure-lsp never advertises that it wants those notifications.**

## The gap

`ClojureLSP._create_base_initialize_params` (`src/solidlsp/language_servers/clojure_lsp.py:315-347`) declares:

```python
"capabilities": {
    "workspace": {
        "applyEdit": True,
        "workspaceEdit": {"documentChanges": True},
        "symbol": {"symbolKind": {"valueSet": list(range(1, 27))}},
        "workspaceFolders": True,
    },
    ...
```

No `didChangeWatchedFiles` entry. Compare `rust_analyzer.py`, `pyright_server.py`, `eclipse_jdtls.py`, etc.:

```python
"didChangeWatchedFiles": {"dynamicRegistration": True, "relativePatternSupport": True},
```

I audited every server that builds initialize params — **14 of 73 declare it, 59 do not**, and `clojure_lsp.py` is in the second group (`gopls`, `typescript_language_server`, `ruby_lsp`, `zls` and others are too). I also checked `DefaultInitializeParamsBuilder` (`src/solidlsp/initialize_params.py`): it only injects `processId`, `rootPath`, `rootUri`, `clientInfo`, `workspaceFolders` and `initializationOptions` — it never merges in a default `capabilities` block. So nothing supplies the capability on the server's behalf.

Per LSP spec, `workspace/didChangeWatchedFiles` is a client capability the server may rely on to decide whether to register file watchers (and servers are within their rights to ignore notifications for a capability the client never announced). clojure-lsp in particular maintains its own analysis database keyed by file, which is what would go stale.

That fits the reported symptom better than a generic index bug: `make-nested` reported at 206-215 — a comment block that *mentions* `make-nested` — is what you get when the server's stored position for that name predates the file being reshuffled, and 454 is where it actually lives now.

## Why this matches the "several times, but not reproducible" pattern

@opcode81 noting it *"was a real phenomenon during Penpot development; it occurred several times"* but not reproducible on demand is the signature of this class of bug: it needs the file to change **outside** Serena's own edit tools while the LS session stays warm — i.e. a git checkout, a rebase, another editor, a shadow-cljs recompile. A clean session, or edits made through `insert_text_at_position` / `delete_text_between_positions` (which do send `didChange`, `ls.py:1382,1425`), will never show it.

## Two things worth separating

1. **Capability declaration** — small and mechanical: add `didChangeWatchedFiles` to ClojureLSP's workspace capabilities so the notifications Serena already sends are ones the server asked for. Cheap, and testable by asserting the initialize params contain it.
2. **Wrong answers should be detectable** — independent of the cause, a symbol whose `selectionRange` is not contained in its `location.range` is malformed. Serena reads the identifier position from `selectionRange` (`src/serena/symbol.py:320-330`) but slices the body from `location.range` (`SymbolBodyFactory.create_symbol_body`), so a divergence silently yields the right name with the wrong body — the worst failure mode for a coding agent, because the model acts on it. A containment check with a warning would turn this into something visible in logs instead of a silent wrong answer.

I have no JVM/clojure-lsp here so I can't run the end-to-end repro to prove the capability is the trigger — that claim is derived from the code, not observed, and clojure-lsp may still watch files on its own initiative, in which case (1) is correct hygiene but not the cause. (2) holds regardless.

Happy to open a PR for either or both if maintainers want them. @opcode81, if you can still reach a Penpot checkout, the targeted repro would be: warm session → `git checkout` a branch that moves `nodes.cljc` around → `find_symbol` without touching the file through Serena's edit tools.

Thanks @MischaPanch — and keeping #1593 open is the right call. To make that decision cheap rather than open-ended, here is exactly what this does and does not settle, plus a concrete way to close it out.

## What is now settled

- clojure-lsp is told the client sends `workspace/didChangeWatchedFiles`, so the notifications `LanguageServerManager.poll_and_notify` was already emitting are ones the server asked for.
- @ebarkhordar verified the `client/registerCapability` path is handled (`clojure_lsp.py:384`), so a dynamic registration in response cannot go unanswered.
- CI's `jvm` batch includes the `clojure` marker and passed on ubuntu/windows/macos, so nothing in the existing Clojure behaviour regressed.

## What is not settled

Whether the *absent capability* was the cause of the staleness in #1593. No test in the suite sets up the failing shape, because every test edits through Serena's own tools, which already send `didChange`. The bug needs an edit from **outside** Serena while the session stays warm.

## Repro that would settle it

```
1. open a Clojure project, run find_symbol on a symbol in file F   (warms the session)
2. WITHOUT using Serena's edit tools, change F on disk:
      git checkout <branch-that-moves-that-symbol>
   (another editor or a shadow-cljs recompile works too)
3. run find_symbol on the same symbol again, same session
```

Before this change: step 3 could return the symbol's *old* position — in @opcode81's case a comment that merely mentioned `make-nested`, while the real definition had moved to line 454.

After: the mtime poll fires `didChangeWatchedFiles`, and clojure-lsp now has a reason to act on it.

If it still reproduces on `main`, the capability was not the mechanism and the next thing I would look at is whether clojure-lsp actually registers watchers in response, since a server may accept the capability and still decline to watch. Happy to dig into that if it comes to it.

@opcode81 you mentioned this happened several times during Penpot development — if you still have that checkout, step 2 as a `git checkout` between two branches that move a defn around is probably the fastest path to a verdict.

One correction to my own earlier framing, for the record: I described this as "correct protocol hygiene, possibly not the root cause" and that remains my honest position. I would not want the merge read as evidence the staleness is fixed.
Given many improvements in the meantime, I will consider this as resolved. Will reopen if the issue reoccurs.

1552.body:
## Summary

In a Svelte project configured with `languages: [svelte]` (the documented setup), `find_symbol` and `get_symbols_overview` return **empty results for `.ts`/`.js` files**. Because Serena's `find_referencing_symbols` must first locate a symbol via `documentSymbol`, this also makes the documented `.svelte`-aware **find-references unreachable when starting from a `.ts` symbol** — it fails with `No symbol matching '<name>' found` before the companion TS server is ever consulted.

Net effect: in svelte-only mode, symbols that live in plain `.ts` files (services, stores, types, utils — the backbone of a SvelteKit app) are **undiscoverable** through Serena's symbolic tools.

## Environment

- serena-agent **1.5.3**
- svelte-language-server **0.18.0**, companion typescript **6.0.3**, typescript-language-server **5.1.3**, typescript-svelte-plugin **0.3.52** (all default, auto-installed)
- Context: `claude-code`
- Platform: macOS (arm64), Python 3.13
- Project config:
  ```yaml
  languages:
    - svelte
  ```

## Steps to reproduce

In any SvelteKit project (a `.ts` module exporting symbols, imported by several `.svelte` components):

1. Configure `languages: [svelte]` and index the project.
2. `get_symbols_overview` on a plain `.ts` file (e.g. one exporting `class AuthService` and `export const authService = new AuthService()`).
3. `find_symbol` for those `.ts` symbols.
4. `find_referencing_symbols` for one of them.

### Expected

- `get_symbols_overview`/`find_symbol` return the `.ts` file's symbols.
- `find_referencing_symbols` returns usages **including `.svelte` consumers** (per the Svelte config docs: *"find-references from `.ts`/`.js` files correctly include `.svelte` consumers; Serena merges and deduplicates reference results from both servers automatically"*).

### Actual

- `get_symbols_overview` on the `.ts` file → `{}`
- `find_symbol` for the `.ts` symbols → `[]`
- `find_referencing_symbols` → `Error: No symbol matching '<name>' found`

`.svelte` files behave correctly (with `depth=1`, the `<script>` symbols are returned). Only `.ts`/`.js` symbol **discovery** is broken in svelte-only mode.

## Root cause (from source)

In `solidlsp/language_servers/svelte_language_server.py` (v1.5.3), only **three** request methods are overridden to delegate `.ts`/`.js` files to the `.svelte`-aware companion `typescript-language-server`:

- `request_references` (~line 598) — merges + dedupes companion results
- `request_rename_symbol_edit` (~line 629)
- `request_definition` (~line 640)

There is **no override that routes document-symbol requests to the companion**. So `find_symbol`/`get_symbols_overview` (backed by `documentSymbol`) on a `.ts` file are answered by the base `svelteserver`, which only provides `documentSymbol` for `.svelte` files and returns empty for `.ts`/`.js`.

This is why the otherwise-correct `.svelte`-aware find-references can't be used from a `.ts` symbol: the symbol-discovery step that `find_referencing_symbols` depends on never reaches the companion.

Notably, none of the documented Svelte settings (`initialization_options_configuration`, `typescript_version`, `typescript_svelte_plugin_version`, etc.) affect this, since they don't change request routing.

## Suggested fix

Delegate document-symbol requests for `.ts`/`.js` files to the companion TS server, mirroring the existing `request_references`/`request_definition`/`request_rename_symbol_edit` overrides (e.g. override whichever method backs `documentSymbol`/symbol-tree retrieval to call `self._ts_server` for `_is_ts_file(...)` paths). That would let `.ts` symbols be discovered and unlock the already-working `.svelte`-aware reference search from `.ts` symbols.

## Workaround

Use `languages: [typescript, svelte]` (TypeScript first) if you need `.ts` symbol discovery/navigation — but note its `request_references` is then answered by the standalone TS server, which is **not** `.svelte`-plugin-aware, so cross-boundary references into `.svelte` files are missed. There is currently no single configuration that provides both `.ts` symbol discovery **and** `.svelte`-inclusive references.

comments.body: Thanks for the report, that does seem like a bug

`test_svelte_and_typescript_files_in_symbol_tree` should have caught this. It is explicitly looking for symbols that are defined in .ts files (e.g. `Game`). Perhaps it wasn't caught because all the symbols it looks for are actually also defined in .svelte files ...
@opcode81 yeah, that might well be the case. An artifact of the svelte test repo being the example from the sveltekit page, where names tend to be on both sides..
Indeed, `Game` is found in `Counter.svelte`, which imports it. So we should probably look for a member of `Game` instead, which is never explicitly imported.

Serena 1.7.1.dev0 at `701e7c84`, read from the source (line numbers refer to that commit) and reproduced with solidlsp directly where stated; Linux; Python (pyright) and TypeScript.

`StdioLanguageServer` catches `BrokenPipeError`, `ConnectionResetError` and `OSError` around `stdin.writelines` / `flush`, logs "Failed to write to stdin" and returns (`src/solidlsp/ls_process.py:660-667`). 2077.body:
### Summary

`LanguageServerFileChangeNotifier.poll_and_notify` walks the project's source files and stats each one, and it runs on the symbolic tool paths via `LspApi.ls_sync_file_system_changes()`. The cost therefore scales with the size of the repository and is paid **per call**, not per change.

On a repository with ~107,000 tracked files that is a large fixed tax on every symbolic query. I would like to discuss bounding it. Opening an issue rather than a PR, because the sensible fix is a design choice rather than an obvious patch.

### Where the cost is

`poll_and_notify` (`src/serena/ls_manager.py:303`) iterates `self._project.gather_source_files()` and calls `os.stat` on each path. Its own docstring is explicit: *"The dominant cost is the directory walk plus one `os.stat` per tracked file; this is intended to be called before symbolic tool invocations rather than on a timer."*

It reaches the classic MCP tools as well as the REPL, because `LspApiMixin._api()` (`src/serena/tools/symbol_tools.py:28-32`) returns the same `LspApi` that calls `ls_sync_file_system_changes()`.

To be fair to the current code: `gather_source_files` **does** prune ignored directories during the walk (`src/serena/project.py:353-355`), so this is already much better than walking everything. The remaining issue is simply that the surviving set can still be enormous.

### Numbers

Measured on **v1.7.0** against an Unreal Engine 5.8 tree. The polling implementation has since been rewritten, so these describe the problem's scale rather than `main`'s behaviour — that is exactly why I am opening an issue instead of sending the local patch:

- tracked source files: **187,590** before ignore tuning, **107,852** after
- a full walk: **190s** → **59s** after the same tuning
- with a 45s tool timeout, **no symbolic call ever reached the language server**; clangd received zero `didOpen` requests across an entire session

The tuning that produced the second column was ours, in `.serena/project.yml`. The point is that even a well-tuned large repository leaves ~100k files to stat before every call.

### Possible directions

Not sure which you would prefer, and I do not want to guess in a PR:

1. **Debounce.** Skip the poll if one completed within the last N milliseconds. A handful of symbolic calls in quick succession is the common pattern, and they cannot each need a fresh walk.
2. **Watch instead of poll.** `watchdog` is already a dependency elsewhere in the ecosystem; an OS-level watcher turns the per-call cost into a background one. Bigger change, best outcome.
3. **Budget the walk.** Above a configurable file count, poll a subset — for example only directories touched since the last poll — and accept eventual consistency.
4. **Make it configurable.** A `serena_config.yml` setting to disable or throttle the poll for repositories where the trade is not worth it. Least elegant, smallest diff, and unblocks large repositories immediately.

(1) and (4) look like the cheapest useful steps, and I am happy to implement either. (2) is the one I would like to see but it is your call whether that is welcome as an outside contribution.

### Environment

Windows 11, Python 3.13, Serena v1.7.0 where measured; `main` at `bd2712fd` reviewed for the code references above. Repository: Unreal Engine 5.8 source plus three game projects, C++/C#/Python, four language servers configured.

comments.body:
I have now measured this against `main` rather than v1.7.0, and the result corrects the framing in my original post. **The `os.stat` loop is not the problem — it is 8% of the cost.** The walk is, and the walk is not I/O-bound.

Measured on `bd2712fd`, no language server started, calling `Project.gather_source_files()` directly. Windows 11, Python 3.13, 97,549 tracked files, five language servers configured.

### Per symbolic tool call

| | cold | warm |
|---|---|---|
| `gather_source_files()` | 79.14s | 83.24s |
| `os.stat` over the result | 6.95s | 6.96s |
| **total** | **86.09s** | **90.20s** |

The second call is not faster than the first, so every symbolic tool call pays this in full. With a 45s tool timeout, no symbolic call completes.

### Where the 80 seconds goes

| | |
|---|---|
| bare `os.walk` of the whole tree (707,889 files, no pruning) | **10.72s** |
| walk + directory pruning only | 9.55s |
| per-file `is_ignored_path` — 230,021 calls | **63.89s** (278 µs/call) |

The filesystem is not the bottleneck: an unpruned walk of a tree seven times larger than the tracked set takes 10 seconds. The cost is the per-file ignore check.

### Why that call is 278 µs

`cProfile` over 15,000 real calls to `is_ignored_path(..., ignore_non_source_files=True)`:

```
ncalls  tottime  function
 15000    1.401  {built-in method nt._path_exists}
 15000    1.144  {built-in method nt._path_isfile}
 10760    0.863  {built-in method nt._path_isdir}
```

**3.41 seconds of the profiled run is three filesystem calls per path — about 82% of the per-call cost.** They come from `is_ignored_path` determining whether the path is a file or a directory:

```python
exists = os.path.exists(abs_path)
is_file = os.path.isfile(abs_path) if exists else bool(rel_path.suffix)
```

That is a reasonable thing for the method to do when called in isolation. But `gather_source_files` calls it from inside `os.walk`, which has **already** separated `dirs` from `files` — the answer is known before the call is made, and is then re-derived with two syscalls. The remainder is `pathlib` churn: ~180,000 `PurePath.__init__` calls for 15,000 paths.

### What this suggests

A fix looks smaller than any of the four options in my original post:

1. **Let the caller pass what it knows.** An optional `is_file: bool | None = None` on `is_ignored_path`, supplied by `gather_source_files` from the `os.walk` split. Removes two syscalls per path and nothing else changes.
2. **Use `os.scandir`.** `DirEntry.is_file()` is answered from the directory entry the OS already returned, so the classification is free.
3. Reduce the `pathlib` allocation per call, which is the other ~18%.

On this repository (1) alone should take the walk from ~80s to roughly 20s. That does not make an 80s operation cheap enough to run per call — debouncing or watching is still worth having, and is what my original post was asking about — but it is a large win for a small, self-contained change, and it benefits every caller of `gather_source_files`, not just the poll.

I am happy to open a PR for (1), or (1)+(2) together if you would rather do it once. Say which shape you prefer and whether it wants to be one PR or two.

*(For completeness: the numbers in my original post were v1.7.0 and I labelled them as such. Treat the ones here as the real ones.)*

#2078 has implemented (1).

@Volksie shall we consider this resolved, or do you want to implement additional optimisations?

Your 09-18 follow-up corrected the premise — os.stat is only ~8% of the cost; is_ignored_path's three syscalls per path (63.9s of 80s) dominate, so any design starts from the caller-passes-is_file / os.scandir fix: Agreed it's a design choice — invert freshness from poll-per-call to notification-driven invalidation. Tier 1 - subscribe to the language server's file-change notifications; treat its watch as authoritative. Tier 2 - the scandir/is_file-aware walk (~80s to ~20s per the measurements above) with mtime-cached directory state and debounce — a call stats directories on the hot path, not ~97.5k tracked files on main. Invariant: a symbolic tool may run on a snapshot whose staleness is known and bounded - if freshness can't be established within budget, return `stale_snapshot` instead of silently querying old indexes. That converts the per-call tax into amortized O(changes). Want me to take a crack at it? Happy to open a PR with working code.

## option to throttle or disable the per-query file-system poll for a checkout that does not change

**Serena version:** serena-agent 1.7.0 (`uvx --from serena-agent==1.7.0`), Python 3.13.16, Windows 11, MCP over
streamable HTTP, C# project of about 176 projects plus PowerShell and Python.

### What happens

In 1.7.0, seven tools in `serena/tools/symbol_tools.py` call `self.project.ls_sync_file_system_changes()` before
doing their work: `find_referencing_symbols`, `find_implementations`, `find_declaration`,
`get_diagnostics_for_file`, `get_diagnostics_for_symbol`, `rename_symbol` and `safe_delete_symbol`.
(`get_symbols_overview` and `find_symbol` do not.) That reaches
`LanguageServerManager.sync_file_system_changes()` in `serena/ls_manager.py`, which calls
`LanguageServerFileChangeNotifier.poll_and_notify()`. That method walks the whole project, tests every path against
the ignore rules, and compares modification times. There is no configuration option to turn it off or limit how
often it runs.

On a large repository the walk dominates the cost of a query. Measured 7-8 Oct 2026 on one repository, after
tightening `ignored_paths` (which brought an idle walk down from 23.2 s):

| Machine state | Time spent in the walk per symbol query |
| --- | --- |
| idle | 8.5 s |
| under a parallel build | 42 - 103 s |
| overnight, with other background work | 2 - 2.5 minutes |

The MCP client in use times out at about two minutes, so under load a symbol query can fail on the walk alone,
before the language server is asked anything.

### Why the walk is unnecessary in some deployments

We run one Serena as a shared MCP server (`start-mcp-server --transport streamable-http`) for many clients. It
indexes a dedicated, detached checkout that nothing edits, and updating that checkout always restarts the server.
In that setup every walk reports zero changes. Edits made through Serena's own editing tools already notify the
language servers directly, so the poll exists only to catch edits made by something else, and in this setup
nothing else makes any.

### Current workaround

A launcher that replaces the method before starting the CLI:

```python
from serena.ls_manager import LanguageServerManager

LanguageServerManager.sync_file_system_changes = lambda self: 0

from serena.cli import top_level

top_level(args=sys.argv[1:], prog_name="serena")
```

This works on 1.7.0 but depends on a private method's name and signature.

### Proposal

A project or context setting, with a matching CLI flag on `start-mcp-server`, for example:

```yaml
# project.yml
file_change_polling: always | interval | never    # default: always (current behaviour)
file_change_poll_interval_seconds: 30             # used when file_change_polling is interval
```

- `never`: skip the walk. Suits a read-only or pinned checkout, such as a shared server or a CI analysis job.
- `interval`: walk at most once per N seconds, so a burst of queries pays for one walk rather than one each.
- `always`: today's behaviour, and the right default for an interactive session whose checkout is being edited.

Logging the walk's duration at info level would also help, because a slow walk currently looks like a slow
language server. The existing log lines give a start and an end but no elapsed time.

### Minimal reproduction of the cost

1. Point Serena at a large repository (tens of thousands of files) and start the MCP server.
2. Call `find_referencing_symbols` for one symbol in one small file several times in a row.
3. In the log, compare the time between `Polling file system for changes to source files ...` and
   `File system polling complete; 0 change events sent to language servers.` with the time of the whole call.
4. Repeat while the machine is busy with a build. The walk grows far more than the language server's own work does.

I will implement additional improvements that will speed up the file system operations.

## Summary

When two stdio Serena instances activate the **same** project, both spawn an Eclipse JDT language server and hand each one the **identical** `-data` workspace directory. Eclipse JDT workspaces are single-writer by design, so the two servers continuously invalidate each other's index. The result is that neither ever reaches an idle state: they sat at **160% and 128% CPU with 1.4 GB + 2.6 GB RSS** on a single Gradle/Java project, indefinitely, on an otherwise-healthy machine.

Nothing warns the user. There is no lock, no error surfaced through MCP, and no log line indicating the collision — it presents only as the machine becoming slow.

## Relationship to existing issues

I found the prior art and want to be explicit about what is and isn't new:

- **#1235** (*Duplicate Serena instances and unsafe concurrent writes when the same project directory is open in multiple MCP clients*) — closed 2026-03-27 pointing at the documented [single persistent server mode](https://oraios.github.io/serena/02-usage/040_workflow.html#multiple-agents-accessing-a-single-serena-instance). That resolution addresses the *duplication*; this report is about the concrete **unsafe-write mechanism** on the JDTLS side, which remains unguarded regardless of whether the user knows about HTTP mode.
- **#1864** — the same *class* of problem (N sessions racing a single-instance resource) but for the **JetBrains** backend and `DirectoryLock`. This is the **LSP/EclipseJDTLS** equivalent.
- **#937** — `init_language_server_manager` never completing despite JDTLS finishing; possibly a downstream symptom of the same contention.

The argument for treating this separately: stdio-per-session is the **default**, HTTP mode is opt-in, and the failure mode here is silent index corruption plus a multi-GB / multi-core resource leak. A user following the defaults gets no signal that anything is wrong.

## Environment

- Serena **1.2.0** (uv tool), `--context=copilot-cli --project-from-cwd`
- `language_backend: LSP`
- Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, 12-core i7-1365U
- Project: Java/Gradle (`build.gradle`, `settings.gradle`), moderate size
- MCP client: GitHub Copilot app — each session spawns its own stdio Serena instance

## Reproduction

1. With `language_backend: LSP`, open **two** concurrent MCP sessions whose cwd is the **same** Java project.
2. Each activates the project and starts an Eclipse JDT language server.
3. Inspect the `-data` argument of both JDTLS processes.

Both receive the same path:

```console
$ tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/625237/cmdline | grep -A1 -x -- -data | tail -1
/home/sp/.serena/language_servers/static/EclipseJDTLS/workspaces/2269b098e07d8bdba1bd239a2fac6177/data_dir

$ tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/626656/cmdline | grep -A1 -x -- -data | tail -1
/home/sp/.serena/language_servers/static/EclipseJDTLS/workspaces/2269b098e07d8bdba1bd239a2fac6177/data_dir
```

The workspace hash is derived from the project path, so *every* concurrent session on a given project collides on one workspace directory.

Neither settles. Sampled ~5 minutes after start, with the project otherwise idle:

```
pid=625237   160.0% CPU   1428 MB
pid=626656   128.2% CPU   2579 MB
```

## Secondary observation: repeated StackOverflowError in the shared workspace

The same workspace's Eclipse log contains **149 `StackOverflowError` occurrences** across **10 rotated `.bak_N.log` files** (Eclipse rotates on restart, so the workspace has been re-initialised at least 10 times). The stack is regex recursion:

```
java.lang.StackOverflowError
	at java.base/java.util.regex.Pattern$Branch.match(Unknown Source)
	at java.base/java.util.regex.Pattern$GroupHead.match(Unknown Source)
	at java.base/java.util.regex.Pattern$LazyLoop.match(Unknown Source)
	at java.base/java.util.regex.Pattern$GroupTail.match(Unknown Source)
	at java.base/java.util.regex.Pattern$BranchConn.match(Unknown Source)
	at java.base/java.util.regex.Pattern$CharProperty.match(Unknown Source)
```

This looks like catastrophic backtracking on some input file rather than a concurrency symptom, so it may well be a **separate** bug — I'm including it because it shares the workspace and may compound the restart churn. Happy to split it into its own issue if you'd prefer.

## Suggested fixes

Roughly in order of how well they'd contain the failure:

1. **Namespace the JDTLS `-data` directory per language-server instance**, not solely per project path — e.g. append a PID/session/instance suffix. This makes concurrent sessions safe by construction, at the cost of some disk and duplicate indexing.
2. **Reuse a single language server per project across instances** (in-process reference counting), which avoids the duplicate indexing cost entirely and is the semantically ideal fix.
3. **At minimum, detect and warn.** Take an advisory lock on the workspace directory; if it's already held, log loudly and surface an MCP-visible warning rather than proceeding into silent corruption. Even just a startup log line naming the workspace path would make this diagnosable — I only found it by inspecting `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`.

Option 3 alone would have turned this from "my machine is mysteriously slow" into a one-line diagnosis.

## Workaround for others hitting this

Either switch to the documented single persistent server (HTTP/SSE) mode, or avoid concurrent MCP sessions rooted in the same project. To recover after it has happened, stop the orphaned servers and delete the corrupted workspace so it rebuilds:

```bash
rm -rf ~/.serena/language_servers/static/EclipseJDTLS/workspaces/<hash>
```
